summary: Iter289 visual QA (cathy@example.com, web + mobile). Verified 5 of 6 target areas via computed styles + screenshots in BOTH light and dark. WEB PARTICIPANT PROFILE could NOT be verified because /app/participants/{id} now returns a 500 'Something on our side broke' error page — the very route that hosts core1-profile-header, core1-artefacts-grid and core1-timeline-expand is broken (regression from iter288 which reported it as 404 on /app/profile). Everything else looked correct: Account Health ring '11%' is white on the teal gradient (rgb(255,255,255)); Settings billing-participants-card is solid clay (rgb(165,81,43)) with white text; web stream cards have distinct teal / sage / clay soft-tint backgrounds with 4px coloured left accent (borderLeftColor teal rgb(15,86,72) / sage rgb(94,126,99) / clay rgb(160,85,69)) — however the numeric % on each card is muted-grey rgb(82,75,66), NOT the coloured number the spec calls for. Mobile Participant Profile is fully compliant: solid teal banner with white 'Mum's Profile' heading; and all five cards render with the requested soft-tint backgrounds (personal-details teal rgb(220,233,234), financial-position sage rgb(238,243,238), follow-ups clay rgb(243,231,222), latest-activity teal, timeline clay — none plain grey).

ui_bugs.issue: GET /app/participants/{id} renders the '500 Something on our side broke' error page for cathy@example.com (participant id 0c538637-b0dd-4982-8f78-b32814c6a5eb). Only /app/participants/{id}/timeline works. Consequence: NONE of this iteration's participant-profile deliverables can be visually verified — core1-profile-header (teal banner + white text), core1-artefacts-grid (rotating solid tones + white text), core1-timeline-expand (collapsed-by-default) and core1-timeline-list (major events only, clay panel + white text) all rely on this route rendering. Reference: /app/frontend/src/pages/ParticipantProfile.jsx (route handler throws — likely a runtime exception in data fetch/render).

The spec calls for a 'coloured number' per stream (teal/sage/clay). Current numeric % renders as rgb(82,75,66) muted-grey (text-muted-k class) on all three cards in BOTH light and dark. The soft-tint bg + 4px coloured left border are correct, but the number itself is not tone-coloured. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/StreamProgress.jsx (the tabular-nums span uses text-muted-k instead of the tone.solid colour).

parity_issues.issue: Mobile participant profile renders end-to-end (header + 5 tinted cards); web equivalent 500s at the route entry.
parity_issues.expected: Both surfaces render the participant profile with matching colour treatment.
parity_issues.actual: Web: 500 error page. Mobile: fully rendered and compliant.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix the /app/participants/:id route 500 error (ParticipantProfile.jsx). Without this the iter289 primary deliverables (core1-profile-header teal banner, core1-artefacts-grid rotating solid tones, core1-timeline-expand collapsed timeline, panel-solid-clay timeline section) cannot be reached. Inspect server-side console for the thrown exception on GET /app/participants/{cathy_active_participant_id}.
MEDIUM: In StreamProgress.jsx, colour the numeric % text with the stream's tone.solid (teal / sage / clay) instead of text-muted-k. Spec explicitly calls for a 'coloured number' per stream.

LOW: After the profile route is restored, re-run this iteration's participant-profile probes (artefact ARTEFACT_TONES rotation, force-white text, core1-timeline-expand → core1-timeline-list toggle, MAJOR_TIMELINE_EVENTS filtering) in both light and dark before shipping.
critical_code_review_comments: ParticipantProfile.jsx: a 500 on a route that a signed-in caregiver's dashboard links to (via /app/participants/{id}/timeline navigation) is a data-fetch or render exception that also affects the parent /participants/{id} render. Add a defensive error boundary + surface the technical detail behind the existing '500 Something on our side broke' fallback so the actual thrown error is visible in preview.

StreamProgress.jsx: the number colour should track the stream tone (already computed as tone.solid for the border and header). Reusing text-muted-k defeats the point of the new colour treatment and drops the visual hierarchy in dark theme.

success_rate.frontend: ~75% — 3 of 4 web deliverables verified, participant profile blocked by 500; mobile profile verified end-to-end; mobile streams not confirmed in this run.

After the main agent fixes ParticipantProfile.jsx render, re-run: (1) verify core1-profile-header background is teal gradient with white text; (2) core1-artefacts-grid children each have a UNIQUE ARTEFACT_TONES colour bg AND .force-white styling applied (no white-on-white); (3) core1-timeline-section is panel-solid-clay + white; core1-timeline-expand button appears by default, click reveals core1-timeline-list with only MAJOR_TIMELINE_EVENTS. rca of the issue: The web participant profile 500 could not be root-caused from client-side only — the fallback page swallows the exception. Recommended: temporarily log the caught error to the console or expose it in the 'Technical detail' details block so the underlying cause (likely a null-dereference on a new API field consumed by ParticipantProfile.jsx that isn't populated for cathy's active participant, or a routing regression around the newly-collapsed TimelineList) is visible in preview.
